overview_markdown:
MicroClaw is a self-hosted agentic AI platform written in Rust, inspired by nanoclaw and positioned as a lightweight alternative in the OpenClaw ecosystem. It ships three entry points from a single agent core: **MicroClaw Server** for always-on chat channels, web/API access, scheduling, and automation; **MicroClaw Work**, a native GPUI desktop app for local workspace-centered agent sessions; and **microclaw-sdk**, which lets other Rust applications embed the same channel-independent Agent Engine with tools, policy, memory, skills, and runtime events.

Architecturally, it is designed for work that outlasts a single request: multi-step tool use, resumable sessions, durable delivery, persistent memory, scheduled tasks, and governed extensions all run in one runtime. The SDK offers tiered feature sets (`minimal`, `standard`, `full`, `remote-worker`), making it attractive for developers who want agent capabilities inside their own Rust services rather than a monolithic gateway.

Compared to OpenClaw, MicroClaw trades ecosystem breadth for footprint and embeddability. OpenClaw offers a massive skills registry, dozens of chat channel plugins, and a huge community, while MicroClaw is earlier-stage (v0.6.x) with a smaller community, a stable branch recommended over a fast-moving main, and active release discipline visible in recent commits. It is best suited to Rust-centric teams and self-hosters who value a lean, native, local-first agent runtime.
